title: Whether and when gratitude appeals work: the role of online community identity and an other-focused mindset
journal: Journal of Research in Interactive Marketing
abstract: Purpose This research examines whether and when gratitude appeals are effective in online community contexts. It tests whether community identity salience enhances their persuasiveness, identifies the underlying psychological mechanism, and examines community- and brand-level boundary conditions. Design/methodology/approach Across three experiments, this study tests the proposed framework. Experiment 1 examines whether an other-focused mindset mediates the effect of online community identity salience on purchase intention for products promoted through gratitude appeals. Experiment 2 tests community interaction structure (reciprocal vs broadcast-oriented) as a community-level boundary condition. Experiment 3 compares Guochao (China-chic, culturally symbolic) with non-Guochao branding to test a brand-level boundary condition. Findings Online community identity salience increases purchase intention for products promoted through gratitude appeals by activating an other-focused mindset. This indirect effect emerges in reciprocal rather than broadcast-oriented communities, and it is weaker under Guochao than non-Guochao branding. Originality/value This research shows that gratitude-appeal effectiveness depends on the social context in which the message is processed. By integrating online community identity, identity-based persuasion, and gratitude-appeal research, it identifies an other-focused mindset as the mechanism and specifies community interaction structure and culturally symbolic branding as boundary conditions. Treating Guochao as an instance of identity-based brand positioning, the study offers a multi-level account of relational persuasion with implications beyond China.

title: When traditional culture meets digital games: pathways and boundary conditions linking cultural identity to purchase intention
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how cultural identity is associated with purchase intention for paid digital games featuring local cultural elements. In the context of Black Myth: Wukong, it further investigates whether perceived value and immersive experience explain this relationship and whether price sensitivity conditions these associations. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 1,167 mainland Chinese and international gamers were analysed using covariance-based structural equation modelling. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) and cross-sample model comparisons were used to examine group differences. Findings Cultural identity was positively associated with purchase intention, with significant indirect effects through perceived value and immersive experience. In the full sample, price sensitivity weakened the links between cultural identity and both mediators and their indirect effects. Mainland Chinese gamers showed higher cultural identity and perceived value, and stronger direct and indirect effects of cultural identity, than international gamers. The moderating effect of price sensitivity was not significant in the international subsample. Practical implications Managers can strengthen culturally grounded digital products by embedding culturally resonant narratives, symbols and aesthetics into product design, communicating their relevance to target consumers and adopting differentiated value-framing and pricing strategies for consumers with varying levels of price sensitivity. Originality/value This study applies cultural identity theory to paid digital game consumption by integrating perceived value and immersive experience as two distinct mechanisms linking cultural identity to purchase intention and examining price sensitivity as a boundary condition of these relationships.

title: Value conversion in co-branded beverage consumption: customer citizenship behavior and the boundary role of scarcity
abstract: Purpose This study examines the pathways linking symbolic, epistemic, and emotional consumption values with customer citizenship behavior in co-branded beverage consumption, and how scarcity conditions these relationships. Design/methodology/approach An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was adopted. Study 1 analyzed survey data from 573 Chinese consumers with co-branded beverage purchase experience using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Study 2 used semi-structured interviews with 22 experienced consumers to contextualize the quantitative findings. Findings The results identified three significant indirect relationships with customer citizenship behavior: symbolic value through conspicuous consumption, epistemic value through co-creation, and emotional value through co-brand love. The emotional-attachment route showed the strongest indirect effect. Scarcity operated as a selective boundary condition: it negatively moderated the symbolic value–conspicuous consumption relationship, did not significantly moderate the epistemic value–co-creation relationship, and negatively moderated the emotional value–co-brand love relationship, with a small-to-medium interaction effect. Qualitative insights further suggest that scarcity may shift from meaningful exclusivity to purchase friction and emotional disruption. Practical implications Brands should design co-branded beverage campaigns that create symbolic visibility, participatory novelty, and emotional attachment, while managing scarcity to avoid stockouts, unclear rules, and consumer frustration. Originality/value This study extends consumption value theory by identifying pathway-specific value-conversion mechanisms in co-branded beverage consumption and refines scarcity research by showing its selective boundary role.

title: The scientific entrepreneur: an entrepreneurial strategy linking founder resilience to enhanced venture sustainability performance
journal: International Journal of Entrepreneurial Behavior & Research
abstract: Purpose Sustainability performance is increasingly becoming a core commercial requirement for new ventures rather than a peripheral societal responsibility initiative. However, we still lack a more systematic understanding of the role that entrepreneurial micro-foundations and strategies play in achieving superior venture sustainability outcomes. Drawing on the Resource-based View of the Firm and Stewardship Theory, we examine how founder resilience and an Entrepreneurs-as-Scientists (EaS) approach interact in shaping new venture sustainability performance. Design/methodology/approach We test our research hypotheses on a sample from the 2023 wave of the Global University Entrepreneurial Spirit Students' Survey, which includes over 13,000 active founders across 39 countries. Findings The findings demonstrate that founder resilience is positively associated with new venture sustainability performance. We find that the effect of resilience as a psychological resource improving sustainability performance is mediated through the adoption of an EaS approach. Moreover, we provide evidence that founder resilience moderates this relationship, helping founders leverage the EaS approach to strengthen sustainability performance. Originality/value Our study advances understanding of the micro foundations of sustainability-oriented entrepreneurship by identifying the EaS approach as a decision-making mechanism channelling founder resilience into superior new venture sustainability performance. The novelty of this study is its investigation of the dual role of founder resilience in achieving superior new venture sustainability performance: as an enabler of an EaS approach and a moderator of its relationship with sustainability performance.

title: The relationship between AI awareness and thriving at work: exploring the moderated mediation model
journal: European Journal of Training and Development
abstract: Purpose Drawing on the socially embedded model of thriving and the conservation of resources model, this study aims to investigate the relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) awareness, seen as a hindrance stressor, and thriving at work. In particular, it explores how AI anxiety mediates this relationship and how self-efficacy moderates the mediating effect. Design/methodology/approach To securitize the study hypotheses, data were obtained from banking employees via an electronic questionnaire, yielding 320 valid responses. The proposed model relationships were assessed through partial least squares structural equation modeling and process analysis. Findings The results uncover that while AI awareness is not significantly linked to vitality, it is negatively correlated with learning. Furthermore, AI anxiety mediates the direct influence that AI awareness has on dimensions of thriving at work. In addition, self-efficacy acts as a buffer, mitigating the adverse indirect influence of AI awareness on thriving at work through AI anxiety. Practical implications This study highlights the need for organizations adopting AI-driven systems to execute‎ initiatives that mitigate AI-induced stress, thereby fostering employee thriving. It is recommended that organizations offer targeted training and digital literacy programs, alongside interventions designed to enhance self-efficacy, to bolster employee well-being amid rapid technological change. Originality/value This study highlights the need for organizations adopting AI-driven systems to execute‎ initiatives that mitigate AI-induced stress, thereby fostering employee thriving. It is recommended that organizations offer targeted training and revise their role descriptions, alongside interventions designed to enhance self-efficacy, to bolster employee well-being amid rapid technological change.

title: The Digital Divide in Global Communication: Inequality, Governance, and the Contest for Narrative Power
abstract: The spread of information and communication technologies has made connectivity central to global communication, yet the benefits of this transformation are distributed unequally. This article examines the digital divide as a structural feature of contemporary global media rather than a mere gap in hardware access. Drawing on scholarship that treats the divide as a complex and dynamic phenomenon, it argues that the divide operates on at least three intersecting levels: access, usage and skill, and algorithmic and infrastructural power. It then traces how the divide is deepened by the politics of platform governance and by asymmetric control over digital content, and considers how these asymmetries become acute in armed conflict, where the ability to generate, moderate, and frame information is itself a weapon. The article concludes that bridging the divide requires not only connectivity and digital literacy but a redistribution of the power to produce and govern the global media environment.

title: The Application of the Inquiry Learning Model to Enhance Critical Thinking Skills in Science and Social Studies (IPAS) Instruction for Grade III Students at SD Negeri 3 Kota Mobagu
journal: International Journal of Educational Research & Social Sciences
abstract: This classroom action research aimed to improve students' critical thinking skills through the Inquiry Learning model in Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS) lessons on heat energy sources in Grade III at SD Negeri 3 Kotamobagu. The study was conducted in two cycles with 29 students, each cycle consisting of planning, action, observation, and reflection. Data were collected through an essay test based on five of Ennis' critical thinking indicators (Focus, Reason, Inference, Situation, Clarity) and through observation of teacher and student activities. In Cycle I, the mean critical thinking score was 58.10, with classical mastery (minimum category Good, score ≥ 60) of 51.72%; student activity was 66.25% and teacher activity was 71.43%, both in the Good category. After improvements in Cycle II, namely stronger teacher guidance, guiding questions, and greater student involvement in inquiry activities, the mean score rose to 77.76 with classical mastery of 93.10%; student activity increased to 88.75% and teacher activity to 91.96%, both in the Very Good category. Based on the school's learning objective achievement criterion (score ≥ 75), classical mastery rose from 24.14% to 72.41%, which is still below the 75% target. These results indicate an improvement in students' critical thinking after the implementation of the Inquiry Learning model.

title: Wearable sensor-based haptic feedback systems for motor learning and gait reshaping: a review
abstract: Purpose This review aims to examine wearable sensor-based haptic feedback systems for motor learning and gait reshaping, with emphasis on the closed-loop chain from sensing to behavioral change. Design/methodology/approach This structured narrative review used a transparent search boundary. Literature was identified from PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore and Google Scholar for work published from January 2000 to May 2026 using combined terms for wearable sensors, haptic or vibrotactile feedback, biofeedback, gait, motor learning, Parkinson disease, stroke, older adults and foot-progression retraining. Studies were included when they reported wearable sensing, closed-loop or cue-based feedback, gait or motor-learning outcomes, validation metrics or deployment constraints; papers were excluded when they were unrelated to gait, lacked wearable sensing/feedback relevance, provided no usable quantitative or architectural information or duplicated a more complete report. Because outcomes and populations were heterogeneous, findings were synthesized as a structured narrative with quantitative comparison tables rather than a pooled meta-analysis. Findings Across the studies summarized in Table 2, the strongest support is for short-term modulation of stance symmetry, thigh extension, gait speed, arm swing and foot-placement targets; reported effects include p = 0.0493 for stroke stance-time symmetry, 14% stride-length and 18% gait-speed increases in older adults, a 229% arm-ROM increase and 2.4 degrees RMS foot-progression-angle tracking error with ICC = 0.94. One six-week knee-osteoarthritis gait-retraining study also reported a 20% reduction in first-peak knee adduction moment and retention of biomechanical and symptom changes at one month. These heterogeneous values do not support a single pooled effect size because sample sizes, comparators, cue schedules and endpoints differ. Sensor accuracy alone is insufficient; repeatability, calibration, latency, comfort, feedback dose, perceptual load, retention and transfer determine whether closed-loop systems remain useful outside the laboratory. Originality/value The review treats wearable haptic gait training as an integrated sensor-feedback-control problem rather than as a catalog of devices.
